---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Moisture Recycling (Rainfall Pattern Regulation)"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Moisture recycling values the rain that a country's land sends elsewhere. Terrestrial evaporation
supplies roughly 40 to 50 percent of the rain that falls over land, so part of every country's
usable water was made by ecosystems upstream of it, often across a border. The account values
water where it is withdrawn; this service re-attributes the terrestrially-sourced share of that
value to the countries whose evaporation became the rain. The base year is 2019.

⚠ The published total is a **re-attribution of a subset of the water-supply row, never an
addition to it**. The source-side total equals the sink-side total by construction, and the task
raises if they differ.

## Quantity

The WAM2layers country-to-country sink-fraction matrix (Bakels and Wang-Erlandsson): cell
$[i, j]$ is the fraction of column-country $j$'s 2019 precipitation that evaporated from
row-country $i$'s land. A column sums to $j$'s terrestrial-origin share, below one because the
remainder comes from the ocean. Read from the path recorded in `es_parameters.csv` as
`moisture_recycling_sink_fraction_input_path`. Twelve destinations sit below the 0.5 degree
tracking grid and carry all-NaN columns; their water value goes unattributed and the task names
them and it.

## Price

None of its own. The value being re-attributed is the water-supply account's irrigation premium
GEP and domestic GEP by country, read as a staged snapshot from
`moisture_recycling_water_gep_input_path` with the component columns listed in
`moisture_recycling_water_gep_component_cols`.

## Attribution

`moisture_recycling_ecosystem_share` scales the terrestrial evaporation credited to ecosystems.
It is 1 in `es_parameters.csv`, counting all terrestrial evaporation; the transpiration-share
decision that would lower it is open with the group.

## Valuation

`reattributed_water_value` is the whole product:

$$
\text{GEP}_i = s \sum_j M_{ij} \, V_j
$$

where $M$ is the sink-fraction matrix, $V_j$ is destination $j$'s irrigation plus domestic water
GEP, and $s$ is the ecosystem share. The diagonal term is published as the own part (a country's
moisture serving its own water use) and the rest as the export part. The destination-side view,
$V_j$ times $j$'s terrestrial-origin share, is published beside it as
`moisture_recycling_sink_side_value`: the same money read from the other end, which is what makes
the nesting under water supply visible per country.

`collapse_countries_to_r250` reduces the r264 correspondence to one canonical row per country
before the join, and the published table carries every account country, NA where the matrix has
no row.

## Inputs

All paths and parameters come from `es_parameters.csv` under the `moisture_recycling` service key:
the sink-fraction matrix, the water-supply snapshot it re-attributes, the component column list,
and the ecosystem share, each with a source row beside it.
